title: Blackwater Trading Post Land Transfer Act
official_summary:
Blackwater Trading Post Land Transfer Act

This act directs the Department of the Interior to take the approximately 55.3 acres of land of the Blackwater Trading Post in Pinal County, Arizona, into trust for the benefit of the Gila River Indian Community, if the community conveys to Interior all of its interest in the land. The land is made part of the community's reservation.

Further, the act prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust.

summary.headline: A 2022 law directs the Interior Department to hold about 55 acres in Arizona in trust for the Gila River Indian Community, adding it to the reservation.
summary.what_it_does: The law tells the Department of the Interior to take roughly 55.3 acres of land at the Blackwater Trading Post in Pinal County, Arizona, into trust. This happens only if the Gila River Indian Community first transfers all of its ownership interest in the land to Interior. Once in trust, the land becomes part of the community's reservation. The law also bars gaming, such as casino-style gambling, on the land.

who_it_affects.how: The community gains the land as part of its reservation after it transfers its ownership interest to the federal government.
The department must take the land into trust for the community if the transfer condition is met.

who_it_affects.group: Residents and businesses near the Blackwater Trading Post
who_it_affects.how: The land's status changes from community-owned to federal trust land within the reservation, and gaming there is not allowed.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 27, 2022, and the land transfer takes place once the community conveys its interest in the land to Interior.
